Subject: Encryption & KMS options — follow-up and next steps

Hi Olivia / Jeremy,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the encryption and data-handling items we agreed to follow up on and propose next steps so you can share with procurement/security: 

1) In-transit encryption
- All traffic to/from Redwood endpoints is encrypted with TLS 1.2/1.3 (up-to-date ciphers). Mutual TLS is available for private deployments if you need client cert auth.

2) At-rest encryption
- Customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Our hosted control plane stores metadata separately from model I/O.

3) Customer-managed keys (KMS) / HSM
- Options: 
  - Redwood-managed keys (default): we manage KMS keys for convenience.
  - Customer-managed KMS (recommended for regulated customers): BYOK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. We support envelope encryption so we never persist your plaintext keys.
  - HSM-backed key options available for Dedicated/Private deployments (customer-managed HSM or cloud HSM).
- Key rotation: you can rotate keys in your KMS; we support key versioning and graceful rewrap to avoid data unavailability.

4) Data residency
- You can pin data to specific regions; we offer region-restricted endpoints and private deployments for on-prem/VPC.

5) Logging & PII handling
- Audit logs are available with token/route-level granularity.
- PII redaction is configurable at ingestion (we can redact sensitive fields before storing logs).
- Retention: default logs retention is 90 days for hosted; configurable longer retention for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps I propose:
- I will send our latest SOC 2 report and encryption architecture diagram (attached).
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep dive with Vivek (security) and your security engineering team to go over BYOK/HSM flow and contract language we typically provide.
- Marissa / Neha will coordinate procurement timeline and any redlines.

Available times for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed next week 10-12 PT or Thu 2-4 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
—
Marissa Cole

Hi Olivia — great questions, answered inline below. I've also looped in Vivek (security lead) and Neha (AE) to coordinate the SE deep-dive and procurement timeline.
• Supported HSMs / access to key material:
  - Supported: AWS CloudHSM (managed HSM) and customer-managed on-prem HSMs for Private deployments. For BYOK via cloud KMS, we never have access to your raw key material — we use envelope encryption and the customer KMS performs the key unwrap. For HSM-backed keys, we can support a flow where the HSM signs/unwraps within your environment.
• Key rotation and availability:
  - Rotation is handled by the customer KMS. We support key aliases and key versioning; when you rotate, we rewrap data keys with the new master key without requiring downtime. There may be a brief increase in latency during a large-scale rewrap operation, but no customer-visible downtime.
• Logs and PII:
  - By default, application-level logs do not persist full unredacted user messages. We provide configurable ingestion-stage redaction so PII can be stripped before logs are recorded. Audit logs will record metadata (request id, model, route, timestamp, token counts) but not message text unless you opt-in. We can set your account to redact by default.
• Log retention:
  - We can support 365-day retention for audit logs for Dedicated or as an add-on for hosted accounts. I'll have Neha surface pricing and contract footprint for this.
• Contract language / deletion guarantees:
  - We have standard clauses for BYOK and key deletion (we can provide sample language). For Private deployments we can add explicit data deletion SLAs. Vivek, can you confirm recommended contract wording for customer-managed KMS and deletion guarantees?
